notes: #81 ADDITION. content/raws/contracts/contracts.json is untouched -- this file hangs a RUNG requirement off some of its offers, the same shape content/raws/factions/ranks.json hangs off factions.json and content/raws/factions/chapters.json hangs off it again. A gate naming an offer contracts.json does not have is refused at load, by name, exactly like a broker or a patron that file does not have would be -- and `nobody_offers_this` is a DELIBERATE bad id, carried on purpose so that refusal is proved by a case (test_contract.cpp) rather than by the file happening to be correct. Do not remove it. WHAT A GATE IS: `minRank` is a rung on the OFFER'S OWN BROKER'S ladder in ranks.json -- 1 is that ladder's first title, matching FactionLedger::rank()'s own numbering where 0 is not a member at all. An offer nothing here names keeps minRank 0, which means exactly what it always has: the broker's own `needs` field (none/acquaintance/member) is the only gate on it. WHICH OFFERS ARE GATED, AND WHY: only Finch's roofline work, and only the two goods above the roofs' own doorway rung. flower_loft and flower_bath stay open to any sworn Tenant -- ranks.json's own note says the first rung IS what makes him say a word about work at all, and a courier run for a back-room grower is the work that earns that rung, not the work that waits past it. dust_quiet and dust_grey_ledger (Finch's own note: 'worth more than the boat it came on', a grey ledger he will not show a stranger) ask Cutpurse (rank 2) -- the rung ranks.json's own file first opens `fence` on, which is exactly the trust a runner with priced goods and someone else's bookkeeping needs before Finch hands it to them. piece_pawn and piece_wrack -- FETCH work, a job that puts a player inside a named house going through somebody's things -- ask Robber (rank 3), the rung that opens `price` on top of `fence`: the roofs do not send an apprentice through somebody's window. cull's bounty (needs: none) and venn's spirit runs (needs: acquaintance, an attitude gate rather than a membership one) are DELIBERATELY left ungated here: the ward's bounty is public work -- 'no rung, no oath, no favour', test_contract.cpp's own words for it -- and a landlord doing a favour for somebody he does not dislike is not the guild handing out an assignment, so gating it on a guild rung it was never asking for would contradict the reason `needs` has three words instead of two. HOW A RUNG IS EARNED IN THE FIRST PLACE: unchanged by this file. Turning in a contract already moves standing with the broker's faction (dialogue.cpp's TurnIn handler, S6) and the ladder's own skillLevel is earned by the hand doing the work contrabandSkill names; this file only decides which offers a rung is allowed to SEE, never how the rung itself is bought.
